newsitem.title: FRANCE: RALLYING-CONFIDENT MAKINEN GOES FOR THIRD STRAIGHT WIN.
newsitem.headline: RALLYING-CONFIDENT MAKINEN GOES FOR THIRD STRAIGHT WIN.

text.p: Reigning world champion Tommi Makinen, winner of the last two events in this year's calendar, plans to make it three in a row with the Tour of Corsica rally starting on Monday.
The Finn was full of confidence ahead of the three-day event on the Mediterranean island's narrow asphalt roads.
"We have a good car and this rally should suit us although it's true that I don't know the stages that well," said Makinen, who had his first win on tarmac in last month's Catalunya rally.
Subaru dominated the first few rounds of this year's championship while Makinen took time to adapt to the new Mitsubishi Lancer.
But the gifted Finn bounced back by winning in Portugal in March before confirming he was back at his brilliant best in the Catalunya rally.
After five events, Makinen enjoys a comfortable lead in the drivers' standings with 28 points, ahead of Subaru drivers Piero Liatti of Italy and Colin McRae of Britain who share second place with 16.
McRae, who was fighting for the lead in the Catalunya rally when a puncture caused him to drop to fourth, said he was looking forward to closing the gap on Makinen.
"I think it will be another close fought battle," said the 1995 champion. "It's a technical event where it's vital to have everything in balance, but it will definitely be won and lost on tyres."

Former world champion Carlos Sainz of Spain badly needs a win to keep his title hopes alive but he struggled on the tarmac in the Catalunya rally in his Ford Escort and will find it difficult to keep up with the pace.
"That race is tough on men and cars but I love it," said the Spaniard, who won the event in 1991. "The route will be slightly different this year but I'm sure it will be just as demanding."
Organisers agreed to change the race's format to comply with new rules aimed at making rallies shorter and more exciting to follow.
All three stages will start and finish in Ajaccio and it will be the first rally with a total distance of less than 1,000 km.

Local fans will be hoping for fine performances from the two-wheel drive Peugeot cars of Frenchmen Francois Delecour and Gilles Panizzi, who were in impressive form in the Catalunya Rally where they led for much of the opening day.
But Delecour said four-wheel drive cars would be hard to beat on the twisting Corsican roads.
"It will be difficult for us because there are far more tight bends in Corsica and you lose your speed," he said.
"The roads are dirtier, too. We were competitve in Spain but we had straight roads and the asphalt was nice and clean. Here, I really don't think we can beat the cars with four-wheel drive."
